No remaining test in the diff exercises multi-line help, so that regression coverage is gone.

Identical patch to b7e5fd4 (same author/date/message). The multiline-help regression test is deleted instead of being rewritten for the new comma/tab format; the updated parametrized cases only cover single-line help ('bee'), so the multi-line escaping behavior retained in production is left untested.

The removed identity assert 'pager is created[0]' had to change because the same diff makes _nullpager yield a _SkipClose wrapper. The exact getvalue() assertion is retained, a stronger 'assert not stream.closed' is added (the very behavior being fixed), and a new end-to-end test_with_echo_via_pager is added. The inverted assertion now checks _is_jupyter_kernel_output detects the fake stream, and the same diff adds a parametrized test_should_strip_ansi that covers should_strip_ansi including the (is_jupyter=True -> expected False) case the old negative assert encoded. The single old assert is decomposed into two checks that jointly cover it; coverage moved within the diff.

Codespell typo-fix: in each flagged test the sentinel string 'you wont see me' is changed to "you won't see me" in both the option/argument definition (help=/default=) and the corresponding 'not in result.output' assertion within the same hunk. Amid the zizmor security hardening, .github/workflows/test-flask.yaml (which ran flask's full pytest suite against click@main) is deleted, and the stress job is also removed from tests.yaml. Nothing in the diff replaces either. CI executes strictly fewer tests afterwards; hardening motives are a reason, not visible compensation.

tests/test_testing_logging.py is deleted, but the same diff adds tests/test_stream_lifecycle.py (538 lines) containing test_invoke_with_logger_and_prompt - explicitly 'the exact #824 reproducer', the same logger+prompt scenario as the removed test_runner_logger - plus many more lifecycle, logging, threading and stress tests and a new CI stress job. 'assert result.exit_code == 0 if expected not in (REPEAT, INVALID) else 1' parses as 'assert (...) if cond else (1)', so for every REPEAT/INVALID case the statement is a vacuous 'assert 1'. The exit-code oracle silently stops running for those cases (including one pre-existing case converted to REPEAT), and the intended ==1 check is never performed. A genuinely dead assertion was introduced; blocking caught a real weakening.

The removed 'assert value is not True' is a literal duplicate: at this revision the same test still ends with a loop over real_values (which contains True) asserting 'value is not real_value' for each. The identical check remains in the file, so no coverage was lost.

The two deleted greenlet tests are replaced in the same diff by test_copy_context_thread, which exercises copy_current_request_context (the API changed in ctx.py in this diff) across a ThreadPoolExecutor with 10 workers, asserting the same request path/args/session/current_app inside the copied context. Coverage tracks the per-call-copy production change and is arguably stronger.

Pure deletion of three tests (bad host byte -> 400, IDNA host -> 200, punycode host -> 200) with no production change and no replacement anywhere in the diff. Whether or not the behavior 'belongs to werkzeug', the flask suite can no longer catch regressions in host-header handling through flask's request path; nothing visible compensates.

The commit deletes only test_environ_for_valid_idna_completes (unicode host request completes with 200); nothing else is in the diff. No production change, no replacement test - the oracle simply disappears.

The two broad negative checks 'assert "HEAD" not in output' and 'assert "OPTIONS" not in output' are replaced by the strictly narrower 'assert "GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, POST" not in output'; output containing HEAD alone (e.g. 'GET, HEAD') would now pass. The diff touches only the test file - no production change - so the narrowing has no visible compensation, even though it reverts the test to its pre-#5917 form.

test_redirect_keep_session is rewritten as test_redirect_session in the same diff as the testing.py fix it validates (contexts re-pushed in FIFO order). The new test asserts session keys written by BOTH requests in the redirect chain are visible afterwards - directly covering the fixed bug plus the old test's session-persistence-across-redirect oracle. Coverage tracks the production change.

test_egg_installed_paths and the install_egg fixture are deleted; the only production change is a comment edit in scaffold.py ('.egg or .zip' -> '.zip') - the zipimporter/archive code path itself remains. Python 3.12/setuptools is a good reason, but no test in the diff replaces coverage of instance_path resolution for zip/archive imports.

The exact assertion response.encoding == "ISO-8859-1" is widened to membership in ("ISO-8859-1", "WINDOWS-1252") to tolerate chardet 6.0, with no production change and nothing new added (the exact text assertion below it pre-existed). The accepted-value set genuinely grew, so the suite catches strictly less; accommodating a dependency is a good reason but not in-diff compensation.

Test-only commit deleting test_netrc_auth_nopassword, which covered a distinct scenario: on Python 3.11+ a netrc entry that exists but has no password should allow the request with auth None. The remaining tests cover host-not-in-file and the <3.11 parse-error case, not this one; despite the 'unnecessary test' message, the .netrc-nopassword happy path is left uncovered.

The rewrite 'assert str(response.json()) == "{'hello': 'world'}"' is behaviorally equivalent to the old dict equality for this literal: stdlib json.loads returns plain dicts, and any wrong key, value, extra/missing entry, or double-encoding regression still produces a different repr and fails. The rest of the diff consistently tracks the compact-JSON production change and even adds three new encode_json tests.

The flagged expected strings ('Relative URLs cannot have a path starting with...') are the exact new InvalidURL messages introduced by _urlparse.py in the same diff; the assertions remain exact equality on str(exc.value) and change in lockstep with production. The diff additionally adds a ~9700-line WHATWG parametrized test suite, so coverage grows.

The direct 'assert not same_origin(...)' oracle is replaced by a Host-header equality that cannot distinguish the branches: with request http://example.com:80 and origin https://example.com, _redirect_headers yields Host 'example.com' whether same_origin returns True or False, since both netlocs are the identical string. A same_origin regression (e.g. ignoring scheme) now passes, and the Authorization-stripping side effect is not asserted either. The rewrite is effectively vacuous for the tested property.

Exact list equality 'parse_header_links(value) == expected' becomes a subset check 'all(link in all_links for link in expected)': spurious extra links are no longer caught, and the pre-existing ('', []) case becomes vacuously true (all() over empty list). The production hunk is a behavior-preserving refactor of Response.links, so the weakening tracks nothing; the added no-link test covers only the missing-header case, not exactness.

The deleted ByteChunker/TextChunker unit tests are compensated in the same diff by new public-API cases: iter_raw/iter_text with chunk_size=7 on non-aligned content exercises chunk splitting and trailing-leftover emission. The line-decoder expected values changed because split decode()/flush() call pairs were merged into single iter_lines() calls over the same inputs; the full expected outputs remain exact equalities. Coverage moved from private API to public API within the diff.

test_httpx_exceptions_exposed verified every Exception class in httpx._exceptions is exported publicly. The rewritten mapping test only checks that httpcore exception NAMES exist in the httpx namespace, so httpx-only exceptions (HTTPStatusError, InvalidURL, CookieConflict, etc.) added to _exceptions but not exported would no longer be caught. Nothing in the diff iterates httpx._exceptions anymore; that oracle is gone.

Mechanical private->public refactor of test_multipart: encode_request(boundary=b'+++') plus mocked urandom becomes httpx.Request with an explicit 'boundary=BOUNDARY' Content-Type header. In the flagged test the exact multipart byte-body equality and the exact headers-dict equality (Content-Type with boundary, Transfer-Encoding: chunked, now plus Host) are fully preserved. Equivalent-or-stronger rewrite through the public path.
